mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕“音乐”话题，涵盖音乐叙事《梁祝》（Reading）、贝多芬的抗争（Extended reading）和音乐与日常生活（Integrated skills）三个子话题——音乐艺术是高考文化传播类应用文的重点场景，也是雅思艺术教育类议论文的常见命题。

subTopics.title: 乐声里的故事：梁祝
subTopics.desc: 课文乐评：小提琴协奏曲《梁祝》combines Chinese and Western musical elements——a piece that really deserves to be heard。

prompts.task: 你的英国笔友 Lucy 喜欢古典音乐，来信请你推荐一部中国音乐作品。请你写一封回信推荐小提琴协奏曲《梁祝》（Butterfly Lovers），内容包括：1. 作品简介；2. 它的独特之处；3. 推荐聆听的段落或方式。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Lucy,

Since you love classical music, let me recommend Butterfly Lovers, a beautiful violin concerto composed by He Zhanhao and Chen Gang — a piece that really deserves to be heard.

The music tells a classic Chinese love story. When the two lovers first meet, the melody is light and pleasant, as if whispering to the audience; during the most exciting part, it turns dramatic with heavier notes; and finally it ends on a bittersweet note, telling how the couple transform into butterflies and fly away together.

What makes it special is that it combines Chinese and Western musical elements — a Western orchestra speaking with a Chinese accent, so to speak.

Do listen to the final section first. I guarantee you'll enjoy it!

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: as if whispering to the audience
combine Chinese and Western musical elements

prompts.task: Some people think that traditional music of a country is more important than international pop music. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In every country the radio now carries two currents: the songs of the world and the songs of the place. Some argue that a nation's traditional music deserves the higher seat; others answer that international pop is the living music of actual life. My view is that the comparison misstates their roles — traditional music is more important to preserve, precisely because pop needs no help surviving.

The case for tradition rests on what such music uniquely carries. Folk songs and classical forms are archives in sound: their instruments, scales and stories encode centuries of a people's feeling, and once lost they cannot be recomposed. Traditional music also anchors identity — a melody built on familiar folk tunes can move listeners who have never studied it, because it speaks an inherited language. When such works cross borders, they carry their culture with them, opening a country to the world's ear as no press release can.

Defenders of pop music hold equally real ground. Pop is democratic and current: it needs no training to enjoy, gives the young a common language across borders, and much of it is genuinely inventive. Dismissing it as noise repeats the very snobbery once aimed at every new form — including, in their day, the traditions we now revere.

My conclusion is that importance splits by function. Pop owns the present and can defend itself in any market; tradition owns the past and cannot. Public support, teaching and stages should therefore tilt towards traditional music — not against pop, but against forgetting. A country can dance to the world's beat and still remember its own tune.

subTopics.title: 让音乐流淌
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：the tears began to flow、fear and excitement flowed over me、the free flow of emotion——音乐最动人的地方，是让情感自由地流淌出来。

prompts.task: 你的英国朋友 Emma 最近压力很大，情绪低落。请你用英文回信，向她推荐用音乐调节情绪的方法，内容包括：1. 表达关心；2. 说明音乐如何帮助你；3. 提出具体建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Emma,

I'm sorry to hear that you've been under so much pressure lately. Please don't keep everything inside.

Whenever I feel low, I turn to music. As soon as the first notes begin, my worries seem to loosen, and sometimes I let the tears simply flow — and afterwards I always feel lighter. Once, during a hard week, a single song filled me with such warmth that fear and excitement flowed over me at the same time. Music lets our feelings move instead of freezing inside us.

So why not make a playlist of songs that comfort you, and give yourself ten quiet minutes a day just to listen? Let the music flow, and let your heart flow with it.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: fear and excitement flowed over me

prompts.task: Some people believe that learning to play a musical instrument should be a compulsory part of every child's education. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Music surrounds daily life, yet few children learn to make it themselves. Some argue that playing an instrument should be compulsory in schools; others consider it an optional luxury. I largely agree that every child should have the chance to learn an instrument, though I would stop short of forcing it on those with no interest.

The benefits of musical training are well documented and reach far beyond music itself. Learning an instrument develops discipline and patience, since progress comes only through steady daily practice; it sharpens memory and concentration; and research links it to gains in mathematics and language. Just as importantly, music gives children a lifelong outlet for emotion — a way to let feeling flow rather than build up inside — and the confidence that comes from performing before others. Made available to all, such training also narrows the gap between wealthy families who can afford private lessons and poorer ones who cannot.

The case for strict compulsion, however, is weaker. Children differ, and a pupil dragged unwillingly through scales may gain little while resenting every lesson; forcing music can even kill the love it hopes to create. Compulsion also competes for hours with other valuable subjects.

The sensible policy, therefore, is universal opportunity rather than universal obligation. Every school should offer instruments and free tuition, actively encourage participation, and let genuine interest, once sparked, carry each child forward.

In conclusion, while I would not compel reluctant students, I firmly believe that learning an instrument should be within every child's reach — a gift too valuable to depend on the accident of family income.

subTopics.title: 音乐与日常生活
subTopics.desc: 课文自述：the Beatles's music has accompanied me throughout my life——一首歌如何成为一段人生的背景音。

prompts.task: 你校广播站“歌声与心声”栏目征集荐歌信。请你写一封信推荐一首陪伴你成长的歌，内容包括：1. 歌曲及你与它的故事；2. 推荐理由；3. 希望播出的时段。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Editors,

I'd like to recommend a song that has accompanied me throughout my school years.

I still remember the first time I heard it: I turned up the volume and stood staring at the radio, holding my breath and waiting for the first notes. Since then, it has been the background music of my life — it cheered me up after my first failed exam, and kept me company on countless evening walks home.

I recommend it because its message is simple but powerful: bad times, like clouds, pass. May it comfort more schoolmates the way it comforted me.

Could you play it during Friday's evening show, when the week feels longest? Many thanks!

Yours,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people say that music is a good way of bringing people of different cultures and ages together. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Music is often called the universal language, credited with joining hands that politics and vocabulary cannot. I agree with this claim to a large extent — music genuinely dissolves barriers that words maintain — while noting one honest limit: it unites most powerfully in the moment, and moments need help becoming more.

The uniting power of music begins in its medium. Melody and rhythm bypass translation entirely: a lullaby soothes, a drumbeat lifts, a lament aches in every language, because music reaches emotion before it reaches meaning. This is why stadium crowds of strangers sing as one body, why a Chinese concerto about butterfly lovers can move audiences who know nothing of the legend, and why grandparents and grandchildren who share no playlists can still share a dance at a wedding. Music also gives divided groups a face-saving meeting place: choirs and orchestras of former enemies have rehearsed reconciliation that negotiators could not draft.

The limit, however, is worth stating plainly. Shared feeling is not yet shared understanding: a festival crowd swaying together returns home to its separate prejudices, and the warmth of a concert, like the concert itself, can end at the exit. Music opens the door between cultures and generations; it does not, by itself, walk anyone through.

My conclusion is that the claim is true and incomplete. Music is the fastest bridge we possess between different peoples and different ages — the cheapest, too, requiring no visa and no vocabulary. But bridges only matter when crossed both ways, and crossing remains work that people, not songs, must do.

subTopics.title: 无声世界的交响：贝多芬
subTopics.desc: 课文传记：almost completely deaf 的贝多芬 never abandoned hope——用铅笔“听”钢琴，让决心 coursing through the music。

prompts.task: 你校英文报以 "Never Give Up" 为主题征文。请你以贝多芬的故事为例写一篇短文，内容包括：1. 他遭遇的困境；2. 他如何应对；3. 这个故事给你的启示。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Never Give Up

When we talk about never giving up, no story moves me more than Beethoven's.

By the time he was a teenager, he had already enjoyed a reputation as a wonderful young musician. Then came the cruellest blow for any composer: he began to lose his hearing. Yet even in his darkest moments, Beethoven never abandoned hope. When composing at the piano, he would put one end of a pencil in his mouth and place the other end against the instrument, so that he could feel the notes through his teeth.

At the première of his Ninth Symphony, he was almost completely deaf — yet the music, full of desperate lows and uplifting highs, still shook the world.

Fate may take something from everyone; what matters is what we create with what remains.
vocabHints: what we create with what remains

prompts.task: Some people believe that difficulties and setbacks help people develop stronger characters, while others think they mainly cause harm. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Whether hardship builds people or breaks them is a question as old as misfortune itself. One tradition celebrates adversity as the forge of character; another warns that suffering mostly wounds. Having weighed both, I believe adversity can strengthen — but only when certain supports are present, which means the second view deserves more respect than proverbs allow it.

The forging view has famous evidence on its side. History's most moving achievements are disproportionately the work of people who lost something first — composers writing against deafness, athletes rebuilt from injury — and psychology recognises the pattern as real: those who survive difficulty often report sharper priorities, deeper empathy and confidence with a foundation, because it was tested. Struggle also teaches what comfort cannot: resourcefulness is learned only where resources end.

Yet the harm view guards an important truth that success stories hide. For every figure who transformed suffering into symphonies, uncounted others were simply worn down — their setbacks brought not wisdom but exhaustion, debt and quiet withdrawal. Adversity's lessons, moreover, are regressive: those with savings, health and supporters can convert a blow into a comeback, while the most vulnerable receive only the blow. To preach that hardship ennobles, without providing help, is comfortable cruelty.

My conclusion is that adversity is a harsh teacher whose classes only some can afford to attend. It can indeed build strength — the deaf composer proves the ceiling — but the survivors' gallery must not hide the casualties. The right response is neither to seek hardship nor to fear it, but to meet it accompanied: supported people grow where abandoned people break.
